### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **51** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via /forms/:slug (route, bridged from symbol servedLabel — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/ui/public-data-collection.mdx`  _(via /forms/:slug (route, bridged from symbol servedLabel — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via /forms/:slug (route, bridged from symbol servedLabel — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via /forms/:slug (route, bridged from symbol servedLabel — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via /forms/:slug (route, bridged from symbol servedLabel — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **20** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 22438726f35d0aa868f8c7570eac8d3fa2761302` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6d5531aa2828645c657a679b5eebcf6e147df437` — the merge of head `26132ae3c256b3525a0c1c09676207e8bdaaaa20` into base `22438726f35d0aa868f8c7570eac8d3fa2761302`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6d5531aa2828645c657a679b5eebcf6e147df437 && git checkout 6d5531aa2828645c657a679b5eebcf6e147df437
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 22438726f35d0aa868f8c7570eac8d3fa2761302 26132ae3c256b3525a0c1c09676207e8bdaaaa20 && git checkout -B drift-repro 22438726f35d0aa868f8c7570eac8d3fa2761302 && git merge --no-ff 26132ae3c256b3525a0c1c09676207e8bdaaaa20

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 22438726f35d0aa868f8c7570eac8d3fa2761302
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 22438726f35d0aa868f8c7570eac8d3fa2761302` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `26132ae3c256b3525a0c1c09676207e8bdaaaa20`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line on the changeset and the PR body is true and complete against the diff. New: the `summary` subcommand (`objectstack-scenarios summary` through `src/bin.ts`, `run-scenarios summary` through `cli.ts`) with `--card` / `--mode`; the module `src/runner/summary.ts` re-exported through `./runner` (`export *` in `src/runner/index.ts`) with every export the line names; `withSuppliedTemplate` and the re-exported `summaryMain` on `cli.ts`; and the run record's optional top-level `template: { file, sha256 }` (ruling B, claim amendment 6907482043). `src/bin.ts` is where the published bin routes its subcommands, so touching it is the order's "only if subcommand routing lives there" case.

The answer that moves is confined to new paths. `run` writes `template` only when a template or ask mode installed the `--template` file (`withSuppliedTemplate` checks `ModeRun.template.source === "supplied template"`); a run without `--template` writes the record byte for byte as before, and a gallery export of a record carrying the key is unchanged apart from the key itself (pinned). `summary` reads files only (no model, no network, cloud#3600), parses records loosely so a field a record predates reads `not recorded`, groups one table per card × mode, and refuses a table whose runs differ in prompt choice, package source, ask repeats or driver, naming each side, with exit 1 while other tables print. A template/ask row is the supplied file (by hash) or that run's scratch author; a record without the key is its own row, never summed. Ask cost and time are summed only when every run of a cell stated them.

### ② Semver level

Patch, as the changeset bumps it. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds: no spec key, app metadata or card JSON changes. The widening is a new subcommand, new exports and one optional record key of the evaluation package `@objectstack/scenarios`. No existing export is removed or narrowed.

### ③ Boundary flags

None. No `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, no platform runtime or security behaviour. `orchestrate.ts`, `scorecard.ts`, `src/score/**`, `schema.ts` and `src/export/**` source are untouched; no grader verdict moves.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-zsupce`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qiby1cctpVpRbJzjccvY`

**VERDICT: PASS**
